facts.raw_span: 2 progressively enlarging, painless nodular lesions on the forehead and right cheek
initially observed as erythematous nodules 3 months prior
lesions gradually increased in size with subsequent central ulceration and blackish crusting
No fever, pain, or discharge from the lesions was noted
history of kidney transplant in 2004 causing immunocompromised status
Two distinct lesions measuring 2 × 2 cm each were identified over the glabella and right cheek
lesions were firm with central ulceration with hemorrhagic crusting
Dermoscopy showed arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment
Extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified
Computed tomography of chest and abdomen showed no involvement of internal organs
Patient had history of kidney transplant in 2004

concepts.why: The patient's immunocompromised status and the presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos in the histopathological examination support the diagnosis of Cryptococcosis.
The presence of skin lesions with central ulceration and hemorrhagic crusting, along with the dermoscopy findings, support the diagnosis of cutaneous cryptococcosis.
The patient's history of kidney transplant and immunocompromised status increase the risk of opportunistic infections, such as cryptococcosis.
The presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos in the histopathological examination supports the diagnosis of a fungal infection.
The patient presented with progressively enlarging, painless nodular lesions on the forehead and right cheek, which were initially observed as erythematous nodules.
The lesions gradually increased in size with subsequent central ulceration and blackish crusting, and were firm with central ulceration with hemorrhagic crusting.
The patient presented with skin lesions on the forehead and right cheek, which were identified as distinct, well-defined, umbilicated skin-colored lesions.
The patient's immunocompromised status and the presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos in the histopathological examination support the diagnosis of an opportunistic fungal infection.
The computed tomography of chest and abdomen showing no involvement of internal organs helps to rule out disseminated cryptococcosis.
